claims.explanation: Halcinonide is a glucocorticoid receptor (NR3C1) agonist, and its selective antiproliferative effect across cancer lines most plausibly reflects NR3C1 expression levels and intact glucocorticoid receptor signaling, since glucocorticoids require NR3C1 to transactivate target genes and induce apoptosis in lymphoid and other sensitive lineages. Lines with low NR3C1 expression or loss of receptor pathway components would be protected, while high NR3C1 expression and glucocorticoid-responsive transcriptional programs (e.g., in hematologic, mesothelioma, and certain epithelial lines) would sensitize. Additional modulation may come from lineage-specific apoptotic priming and co-regulators rather than any single driver mutation.

features.basis: Drug target; glucocorticoid receptor agonist requires NR3C1 for activity
Loss-of-function mutations in the receptor would abrogate halcinonide signaling
TP53-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines, consistent with impaired DNA-damage/apoptotic checkpoints enhancing glucocorticoid-induced death
KRAS-mutant lines appear in the sensitive set, possibly reflecting MAPK-driven glucocorticoid receptor dependency
PTEN loss is common in sensitive lines and may amplify PI3K/AKT-dependent glucocorticoid responses
CDKN2A deletion/mutation is frequent in sensitive lines, suggesting cell-cycle deregulation increases glucocorticoid sensitivity
ARID1A mutations recur in sensitive lines, implicating chromatin remodeling in glucocorticoid response
SMARCA4 mutations are enriched in resistant lines, suggesting SWI/SNF loss reduces glucocorticoid receptor transcriptional activity
BRAF-mutant lines (thyroid, melanoma) are overrepresented among resistant lines
EGFR-mutant glioma line KNS81 is resistant, possibly via RTK-driven survival signaling
NF1 mutations appear in several resistant lines, consistent with RAS pathway activation counteracting glucocorticoid effects
STK11 mutations are present in resistant lines, potentially altering metabolic stress responses
